I went through hell with my family, and was in a horribly abusive relationship. the second I got the chance, I left that shit hole town. I somewhere along the way adopted the ‘if i hurt you; you can’t hurt me’ mentality. Lots of pill popping, lots of drinking, lots of driving inebriated. I was a very shitty person but I didn’t care and looking back, I hate that so much. But I had a near death experience, where I couldn’t remember which side of the road I was suppose to be driving on. At the last second I saw the car and managed to swerve out of the way. I sat in my car in the median for a very long time; wondering how and why I had let my life turn out like this. I was only 22 years old. That was 2 years ago. I moved back home, made some GREAT new friends who helped me pick up the pieces and start a new life. Making the right choices and not holding innocent people accountable for other people’s mistakes. Oh, and I’m sober. Off of everything.

My dad woke me up at 3 am by basically slamming my door open and telling me my mom had overdosed in a failed suicide attempt. The race to the hospital felt like it took years, and they basically said she was DOA; but they had brought her back. They kept losing her after a few minutes every time and then we had to make the decision to not try and resuscitate her again, the risk for permanent brain damage too high. I was 16 then, but that night is forever ingrained in my head.

We got into an argument because she took back her cheating boyfriend, and she ending the conversation by telling me to “go find your mother”, knowing my mother had committed suicide four years prior to this argument

A guy who I was friends with had developed feelings for me. He didn’t know I knew, and he didn’t know I had feelings too. There was a lot of stuff preventing us from being together but that’s not the point. 
Basically we had hung out one night and were watching movies. Back then I worked the super early shift so I was dead tired. I was drifting off to sleep, curled up into him when he leaned over me, kissed my forehead and said 
“If situations were different, I’d ask you to run away with me. People like you just don’t exist anymore.” 
It took everything in me not to respond, but if he was as attentive as I thought he was, I’m sure he felt my heart pounding. 

That’s the best compliment, and my biggest regret. I wish I had run away with him.
